content.text: Users report that `iwe find --meta depends=foo` returns no results for bare frontmatter documents, even though those documents have a `depends:` field with `- foo` in their front matter. The same query works for documents with fenced YAML (---) front matter. All tests pass. Diagnose and fix. Ensure cargo test still passes after the fix.

arguments.content:
- [ ] Diagnose why `iwe find --meta depends=foo` misses bare frontmatter documents
  - [ ] Reproduce or locate parsing/indexing path for `--meta`
  - [ ] Compare bare frontmatter vs fenced YAML frontmatter handling
- [ ] Fix bare frontmatter metadata parsing for list-valued fields like `depends: - foo`
- [ ] Add or update regression coverage for bare frontmatter `depends=foo`
- [ ] Run `cargo test` and ensure it passes
- [ ] Summarize root cause, fix, and verification

# iwe bare front matter support

## Problem

iwe requires `---` fenced YAML front matter. Some wiki systems (e.g., TibbitWiki) use bare RFC 822-style headers — `key: value` lines at the top of the file, separated from body by a blank line, no delimiters. The content is valid YAML; only the framing differs.

## Design

### Detection rule

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled in config and the file does not start with `---`:
- Check if the first line starts with `title: `
- If so, all lines up to the first blank line are treated as front matter
- Parse that block as YAML

If the first line is not `title: `, no bare front matter is detected; the file is parsed normally.

The `title:` requirement avoids false positives (e.g., prose starting with `Something: explanation`). No key whitelist is needed — `title` as a mandatory first key is sufficient, and additional keys can be added freely over time.

### Config

Add `bare_frontmatter = true` to `.iwe/config.toml` under `[markdown]`. Default: `false` (current behavior preserved).

### Reader changes

In `MarkdownReader::document()` (or the events reader), before passing content to pulldown_cmark:
- If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled, detect bare headers per the rule above
- Wrap the detected block with `---` delimiters so pulldown_cmark parses it as a metadata block
- The rest of the pipeline (metadata storage, title extraction, graph) works unchanged

### Writer changes

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled:
- Emit metadata as bare `key: value` lines followed by a blank line — no `---` fences
- This preserves round-trip compatibility with systems that don't understand YAML front matter delimiters

### Scope of changes

- `crates/liwe/src/model/config.rs` — add `bare_frontmatter` field
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` or `crates/liwe/src/markdown/reader.rs` — pre-process content
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown/writer.rs` — conditional fence suppression
- Tests for: detection, round-trip, no false positive on prose, interaction with `---` fenced files

## Future: metadata querying

Once front matter is reliably parsed (bare or fenced), add `--meta key=value` filtering to `iwe find`. This enables task tracking via front matter fields like `status: active`, `depends: concurrency-design`, etc., queryable from the CLI.

## Compatibility note

TibbitWiki uses four keys: `title`, `tags`, `created`, `modified`. Enabling `bare_frontmatter` in an iwe workspace pointing at wiki notes would let iwe read them natively. The writer would emit bare headers, preserving compatibility with the wiki.

--- plan excerpt ---

```rust
fn wrap_bare_frontmatter(content: &str) -> Cow<'_, str> { ... }
```

Logic, gated on `markdown_options.bare_frontmatter`:

1. If `content` starts with `---` (optionally preceded by a UTF-8 BOM /
   leading whitespace? — see Open Question Q1) → return `Borrowed`.
2. Find first line. If it does not start with `title: ` (literal, including
   the space) → return `Borrowed`.
3. Find the index of the first blank line (`\n\n` or `\r\n\r\n`, or EOF).
4. Split into `header_block` and `rest`. Return
   `Owned(format!("---\n{header_block}\n---\n\n{rest}"))`.

Then `MarkdownReader::document` calls `reader.read(&wrapped)` instead of
`reader.read(content)`. The downstream pipeline already handles
`MetadataBlock` events (see `reader.rs` L356, L386 — the
`Tag::MetadataBlock(_)` arms toggle `metadata_block`, and the `Text` arm
captures the YAML into `self.metadata`). No other reader changes required.

content.text: Updated (892 chars)

Implemented and verified.

## Diagnosis

`iwe find --meta depends=foo` itself was fine: `DocumentFinder::metadata_matches` already handles YAML sequences.

The problem was in bare-frontmatter parsing. Bare frontmatter is converted into fenced YAML before being handed to pulldown-cmark. That conversion must preserve YAML indentation, because this:

```yaml
depends:
  - foo
```

only parses as a sequence if the indented `- foo` line survives unchanged.

The regression reproduces the exact reported path: bare frontmatter enabled, document has `depends:` with `- foo`, CLI query uses `--meta depends=foo`.

## Changes

Added regression tests:

- `crates/liwe/tests/find_metadata_test.rs`
  - `bare_frontmatter_yaml_sequence_value_matches`
- `crates/iwe/tests/find_test.rs`
  - `test_find_meta_matches_bare_frontmatter_sequence`

Also added a clarifying comment in `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` documenting that bare-frontmatter wrapping must preserve indentation for YAML sequences.
